short: The only woman to rule China as emperor in her own name.
full:
Wu Zhao entered the palace as a junior concubine of Emperor Taizong and, after his death, returned as a consort of his son Gaozong, becoming empress in 655. As Gaozong's health failed she ran the government in his name, and after he died in 683 she deposed one son and installed another as a figurehead. In 690 she ended the pretence, declared her own Zhou dynasty and took the imperial title. The dates here cover that reign; her effective power began some thirty years earlier.

She governed through men she had promoted herself, widening the examination route into office and holding palace tests in person, and through a secret police apparatus that destroyed the old northwestern aristocratic families by denunciation and execution. She spent heavily on Buddhist patronage, including the colossal Vairocana at Longmen. In February 705, aged eighty-one and ill, she was forced to abdicate by a palace coup that restored the Tang; she died that December. Her tomb stele was left deliberately blank.
